findings.issue: stem extraction via `awk '{print $1}'` does not sanitize regex metacharacters. A stem like '.*' would produce RE ^migrations/(.*)\. sql$ (matches all migrations). This is an over-exclusion path, not a shell-injection path (grep -E patterns are not evaluated as bash). Shell injection ($(cmd), backticks) is fully neutralized because the string is only passed to grep as a pattern, not eval'd. Pipe injection (030|migrations/.*) is neutralized by the ^migrations/( ) anchor — the content inside the group sees only the filename tail, not the full path, so a pipe-extended group cannot reach a different prefix. The only practical regex-injection is '.*' or similar wildcards that over-exclude within migrations/. Every such entry is a visible line in the PR diff.
findings.suggestion: Optional hardening: add stem validation (e.g. `[[ "${stem}" =~ ^[0-9]+_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ ]]`) before appending to the array. This closes the wildcard over-exclusion path and is one line. Not blocking because the PR diff is the primary mitigation at the agreed threat model (enforcement.md §7: erring agent, not adversary).

findings.issue: The `# T-XXXX` attribution comment in each data line is documentation only — there is no automated enforcement that the attributed T-ID matches the task that wrote the line. This is intentional (matching the residual-risk posture of T-0146/R-2), but worth noting explicitly in the file header for future reviewers.
findings.suggestion: Add one sentence to the file header: 'Attribution comments (# T-XXXX) are informational; enforcement relies on PR review.' Already implicit; call it out.

role_gap_evidence: NEW VECTOR JUDGMENT (T-0164-B2 specific, axis 5 / enforcement.md §7): The .txt data file is writable by any task without T-0146 meta-gate (T-0146 glob covers only ci/checks/[^/]+\.sh). A task could add any migration stem (including '.*') to over-exclude migrations from the T-0040 frozen-diff check. HOWEVER: (1) The T-0040 frozen-diff check is task-specific — it verifies that T-0040's own branch did not touch foundation files or add migrations. Over-excluding a sibling migration from T-0040's check does not hide that migration from its own task's isolation check (dual-control-isolation.sh, invoke-grant-isolation.sh, etc.) which run independently. (2) A wildcard '.*' stem in the .txt would be a visible, anomalous line in the PR diff — detectable by any reviewer. (3) The threat model is enforcement.md §7: erring/drifting agent, not an adversarial actor. An erring agent adding a spurious stem is visible in PR review, same class of residual risk as T-0146/R-2 (branch-name spoof also requires a reviewer to catch the mismatch). VERDICT ON VECTOR: proportionate mitigation. Attribution `# T-XXXX` per line + PR review constitutes the same detection layer as T-0146's documented R-2 residual. The vector does not enable hiding a migration from all gates simultaneously — only from T-0040's single check. Acceptable at the defined threat tier. No blocking finding.
